items.title: 52193_Jay McShann oral history interview
items.q: So the union sent a guy by the name of Ross L. Claxton out there... So Claxton says, 'Well, he's not in the union and so the union sent me out.'

ctx.x: And he saw this write-up and so he called down to the union. See, but I wasn't in the union then. Called down to the union and told them, says, "Listen, send that musician, have him to get in touch with me and come out to my place out here and get in touch with me." And so the union sent a guy by the name of Ross L. Claxton out there. So when Ross came out to Mr. Bales' place, Mr. Bales says, "Are you Jay McShann?" He says, "No, I'm Ross L. Claxton." He says, "Well, no, I didn't send for you. I told them to send…

So Walter Bales said, 'Well, here,' he gave him some money for his troubles and 'here's your cab fare,' and you know. So Walter Bales called back down to the union next day and says, 'Listen, why is it you guys sent somebody else? I asked you to send McShann out,' you know. So then they made an excuse. They said, 'Oh, we'll get in touch with him and we'll have him to come out. But he wasn't a member of the union, and that's the reason we did that.' So, okay, so finally they contacted me and told me to go out and…
